kill_fact: The terminal-moat default stands unrescued on primary sources, the load-bearing cheapness figure is false, and the entry anchor is stale. (1) TERMINAL MOAT: the deterministic erosion screen (earns below cost of capital, value-destroying) is CONFIRMED by primaries, not rebutted. FY2025 results (24-Feb-2026 release): net loss Group share EUR2,091m including EUR920m goodwill impairments (Lighting, Clarion Electronics), EUR578m capital LOSS crystallized on the planned Interiors divestiture, EUR209m Symbio write-down, EUR135m deferred-tax write-off -- EUR1.84bn of one-off charges are management's own admission that carrying values do not clear cost of capital. The company sold Interiors to Apollo at 3.1x 2025 adjusted EBITDA -- primary-source proof its assets clear at distressed multiples. Operating margin +40bps to 5.6% is restructuring cost-out (EU-FORWARD + Simplify) against contractual OEM price-downs; the FY2025 release contains zero ROCE or pricing-power disclosure, no dividend proposed, and ROIC (~3.5%) remains far below any plausible WACC. No primary evidence of durable pricing power or rising returns above cost of capital exists, so the moat-erosion kill stands. (2) STALE ANCHOR: the debate priced the name at ~EUR8.7; FRVIA.PA trades ~EUR10.1 on 02-Jul-2026 (+16% vs anchor, 52wk range 6.66-15.03). From EUR10.1 the modeled base case (EUR15) is +48% and the modeled adverse SOP (EUR5) is -51% -- the claimed 1.7:1 risk/reward is now ~1:1 against a fat left tail (EUR6.0bn net debt over a ~EUR2.0bn equity sliver). (3) The one clean catalyst (Apollo Interiors, signed 27-Apr-2026) is real but NOT closed: pending employee-representative consultation plus regulatory clearances across 19 countries, closing targeted H2/year-end 2026, and the '>=EUR1bn' debt cut is stated net of minorities, working-capital/pension adjustments, carve-out and tax costs -- a capped, dated, slippable deleveraging arb on a sub-WACC base, not a re-rating of a durable business.
